result.topic_en: From Ramanujan's work on highly composite numbers for the generalized divisor function sigma_{-s}(N): the page determines the exponents a_lambda and the primes P_r for the extremal numbers N, and starts an upper bound for sigma_{-s}(N).
result.transcription:
(311) $a_\lambda = \left[\dfrac{\log\left(\dfrac{\lambda^\epsilon - \lambda^{-s}}{\lambda^\epsilon - 1}\right)}{s\log\lambda}\right].$   Add Ms a 94 18 (41)   (41)   (77)
Hence $N$ is of the form
(312) $2^{\left[\frac{\log\left(\frac{2^\epsilon - 2^{-s}}{2^\epsilon - 1}\right)}{s\log 2}\right]} \; 3^{\left[\frac{\log\left(\frac{3^\epsilon - 3^{-s}}{3^\epsilon - 1}\right)}{s\log 3}\right]} \cdots\cdots\cdots p_1,$
where $p_1$ is the prime defined by the inequalities (308).
61. Let us consider the nature of $p_r$. Putting $\lambda = p_r$ in (306),
and remembering that $a_{p_r} \geq r$, we obtain
(313) $p_r^\epsilon \leq \dfrac{1 - p_r^{-s(1+a_{p_r})}}{1 - p_r^{-s a_{p_r}}} \leq \dfrac{1 - p_r^{-s(r+1)}}{1 - p_r^{-sr}}.$
Again, putting $\lambda = P_r$ in (307), and remembering that
$a_{P_r} \leq r-1$, we obtain
(314) $P_r^\epsilon > \dfrac{1 - P_r^{-s(2+a_{P_r})}}{1 - P_r^{-s(1+a_{P_r})}} \geq \dfrac{1 - P_r^{-s(r+1)}}{1 - P_r^{-sr}}.$
It follows from (313) and (314) that, if $x_r$ be the value
of $x$ satisfying the equation
(315) $x^\epsilon = \dfrac{1 - x^{-s(r+1)}}{1 - x^{-sr}},$
then $p_r$ is the largest prime not greater than $x_r$. Hence
$N$ is of the form
(316) $e^{\vartheta(x_1) + \vartheta(x_2) + \vartheta(x_3) + \cdots\cdots},$
where $x_r$ is defined in (315); and $\sigma_{-s}(N)$ is of the form
(317) $\Pi_1(x_1)\,\Pi_2(x_2)\,\Pi_3(x_3) \cdots\cdots\cdots \Pi_{a_2}(x_{a_2}),$
where
$\Pi_r(x) = \dfrac{1 - 2^{-s(r+1)}}{1 - 2^{-sr}} \cdot \dfrac{1 - 3^{-s(r+1)}}{1 - 3^{-sr}} \cdots\cdots \dfrac{1 - p^{-s(r+1)}}{1 - p^{-sr}},$
and $p$ is the largest prime not greater than $x$.
[-62.-] It follows from (304) and (305) that
(318) $\sigma_{-s}(N) \leq N^\epsilon \dfrac{\Pi_1(x_1)}{e^{\epsilon\vartheta(x_1)}} \dfrac{\Pi_2(x_2)}{e^{\epsilon\vartheta(x_2)}} \dfrac{\Pi_3(x_3)}{e^{\epsilon\vartheta(x_3)}} \cdots\cdots$
for all values of $N$, where $x_1, x_2, x_3, \ldots$ are functions of $\epsilon$

methods.what: Explicit formula for the exponent of prime lambda in an extremal (generalized highly composite) number for sigma_{-s}
Prime factorization form of N, built from these exponents
Characterization of p_r as the largest prime not exceeding the root x_r of an equation
N expressed via Chebyshev theta function
sigma_{-s}(N) expressed as a product of partial Euler-type products Pi_r
Upper bound for sigma_{-s}(N) valid for all N
